messages:
anna: Quick note: running the node sampleapp against staging I hit an intermittent SSE parse error after a reconnect. Error: 'Unexpected end of JSON input'.

liam: Is this the new streaming helper or the old eventsource wrapper?

anna: It's the streaming helper in examples/node. Happened when a long `data:` line was split across the disconnect and reconnect. Raw chunks saved with --sse-raw show boundary fragments.

reza: Can you paste the raw capture? and node version?

anna: Node 18.16.0. Capture excerpt: ```
data: {"op":"patch","payload":"first-half-of-blob"}


data: {"op":"patch","payload":"second-half"}
``` after resume we got leading blank lines and the parser treated it as an empty event which dropped the associated id.

mina: Our parser currently does `buf.split('\n\n')` which breaks when separators cross buffer boundaries. Need a line-oriented state machine: keep partial line, emit on CRLF/LF, and only on an empty full line emit the event.

liam: Also ensure we preserve `id` between chunks and send `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect. For a quick mitigation, ignore entirely empty events (all whitespace) rather than trying to parse them.

anna: I'll prototype a change: incremental line parser + skip-empty-events + add a small netem integration test that simulates a drop mid-data. I'll include the failing capture and enable `--sse-raw` in CI for that test.

ci-bot: Created issue #4198: "sse: incremental parser + netem regression test" and kicked off a focused CI run for branch anna/sse-incremental-parse.

reza: Once PR is ready, add a cross-sdk parity test (node/browser/python) to streaming-parity so we catch this elsewhere.

anna: Will do. Thanks!
